content.text: Typical: S. pneumo · H. flu · M. catarrhalis - RF: COPD · recent influenza · EToH use d/o - advanced age → ↑severity & mortality - most often summer/early fall · common in school-aged children
Atypical: M. pneumoniae · C. pneumoniae · Legionella · viruses (influenza A/B · rhinovirus · RSV · parainfluenza) - M. pneumoniae common in healthy <40y · excellent recovery w tx
•onset in community or <48h after hsp admit - nosocomial >48h after admit to hsp/health care facility
group B strep & E. coli MC
: S. pneumoniae · C. trachomatis · Bordetella pertussis
•viral overall MC: RSV · influenza A/B · human metapneumovirus · adenovirus · parainfluenza · enterovirus D68 · coronavirus · rhinovirus
: S. pneumoniae · H. flu (rare b/c vac) · S. aureus · S. pyogenes · Mycoplasma pneumoniae
· rhinovirus · influenza · parainfluenza viruses · coronavirus · adenovirus
S. pneumoniae · M. pneumoniae · Chlamydia pneumoniae
•cough may be absent initially (few cough receptors in alveoli) - prolonged fever · cough & resp findings ↑likelihood
•most predictive: hypoxemia · retractions · head bobbing · nasal flaring - hypoxia & ↑WOB more predictive than tachypnea, but ⍉tachypnea helps exclude PNA
•younger infants: tachypnea & fussiness rather than cough (↓develop of cough receptors)
: fever + leukocytosis may be only s/sxs
•inspir crackles · bronchial breath sounds (pathologic - vesicular = norm) · focal wheezing (segmental/lobar consolidation)
•consolidation: dullness to percussion (⍉hyperresonance - seen w ↑air in pleural cavity: emphysema · pneumothorax)
•diffuse wheezes → asthma/obstructive dz (generalized airflow obstruct) - fever favors PNA

Typical: sudden fever · productive purulent cough · SOB · pleuritic CP - PE: tachypnea · rales · ↑tactile fremitus · egophony (consolidation) - effusion/empyema → ↓tactile fremitus & dullness - more toxic

Atypical: subacute (days-wks) - low-grade fever · malaise · persistent dry-mildly productive cough · HA · chills · sore throat · wheezing · myalgias · fatigue - extrapulm: confusion · abd pain · diarrhea · rash (M. pneumoniae) - nontoxic · mild pharyngeal infect · nml/mild lung findings (rales · late wheezing) · sinus tenderness
ddx bullous myringitis: historically assoc w M. pneumoniae infect
•atypical: focal segmental → B/L interstitial · hilar adenopathy - bact: focal/lobar
•peds: segmental consolidation · patchy infiltrates · cavitations · effusions
•may be (−) early (lags Sx) → repeat if high suspicion · CT if (−) CXR but CAP Sx
•lung US: B-lines = pathologic interstitial edema (ex, PNA)
•mild uncomp LRTI ⍉need imaging to confirm CAP
: only for hsp pts - severely ill/hsp: CXR · WBC · lytes · acute phase reactants
•CBC w diff · BUN · Cr - then sputum gram stain/cx · blood cx · transaminases · lactic acid · CRP · LDH · PCR
•⍉response to abx: FNA of infiltrate · bronchoscopy w BAL (esp atypicals)
•⍉maintain hydration or feed · RR >50 (>1y) · toxic appearance · virulent organism suspected · ⍉response to outpt tx in 48-72h · preexisting conditions → severe dz
⍉indications alone: abnorm lung sounds · high fever (unless uncontrolled · dehydration or sz)
Tx: empiric antibacterial · antipyretics · hydration - suspected viral → ⍉abx - abx should cover S. pneumo + atypicals
6mo-5y: amoxicillin (suspected bact) or macrolide (presumed atypical) - atypical (Rapid Review): azithro · doxy
•outpt = mild uncomp: T <101.3°F · mild/⍉resp distress · nml color · mental status · feeding & HR · normoxemia
•close f/u w.in 24-48h - abx x7d (≥4mo) except azithro x5d
- >5y w M. pneumoniae/C. pneumoniae Sx: macrolide (azithro · clarithro · erythro) · doxy or resp FQ (moxi · levo)
: adults ≥50 (PCV15 → PPSV23 typically ≥1 yr later), younger pts w conditions that increase the risk for developing comp
Cough may persist up to 4mo - most recover w.o long-term sequelae · ⍉f/u CXR needed
